title: Zero Repeat Regressions: The Golden Metric & The Future of Agentic Trust
why_read: A verbose, buzzword-heavy opinion piece about AI-assisted development trust and metrics, offering anecdote and branding more than rigorous technical evidence.
analysis: This post argues for a metric called 'zero repeat regressions' as a way to measure trustworthiness of AI coding agents, citing a personal ledger of 375 production tickets and referencing Barry Boehm's classic defect-cost curve. The writing style leans heavily on consulting-pitch rhetoric and branded terminology like a '4-Layer Verification Stack' and 'Synthetic Scars' series, without the excerpt showing concrete methodology or data analysis. It touches on a real and relevant topic, trust and verification in AI-assisted coding, but the excerpt itself reads more like marketing than rigorous technical writing. Readers interested in practical AI-coding governance might find value further in, but substance is hard to confirm from what's shown.
